questions.q: List the title of every game in the table.
brief: The table games has the columns title, kind, players and minutes.
Write one query that gives the title of every game.
Print the titles in the order they are stored in the table.
Print each row the query finds on its own line, with the values separated by a single space and nothing else.
questions.starter:
import sqlite3
db = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
db.execute('CREATE TABLE games (title TEXT, kind TEXT, players INTEGER, minutes INTEGER)')

# These lines fill the table for you. Leave them exactly as they are.
rows = []
line = input()
while line != 'END':
    title, kind, players, minutes = line.split(',')
    rows.append((title, kind, int(players), int(minutes)))
    line = input()
db.executemany('INSERT INTO games VALUES (?,?,?,?)', rows)

# Write your query inside the double quotes, then print each row it finds.
# Use single quotes inside the query for any text you compare against.
# for row in db.execute("SELECT ... FROM games"):
#     print(' '.join(str(value) for value in row))
forbid: in rows
The answer has to come from an SQL query. Looping over the rows list in Python does the work the query is meant to do.

tests.why: SELECT names the column you want and FROM names the table. Every game appears because there is no WHERE to narrow it down.
The same query must work whatever is in the table - if this fails you have typed the titles out instead of querying them.
A shorter table, same query. SELECT title gives one value per row, so print that value on its own.

questions.fb: SELECT says which columns and FROM says which table - with no WHERE, every row comes back.
